problem: Is the function $g(x,y,z)=2{x}^{2}+x{y}^{2}+5{z}^{2}$ homogeneous? If so, what is its degree?

feedback.problem: Is the function $g(x,y)=2{x}^{3}+3{y}^{2}$ homogeneous? If so, what is its degree?
feedback.worked_solution:
A function $g(x,y)$ is homogeneous of degree $n$ if it satisfies the property

$$
g(tx,ty)={t}^{n}g(x,y).
$$

So first, we compute $g(tx,ty),$ and then we try to simplify by writing it as ${t}^{n}g(x,y)$ for some $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(tx,ty) & =2(tx)^{3}+3(ty)^{2} \\  & =2{t}^{3}{x}^{3}+3{t}^{2}{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

It's impossible to write this as

$$
{t}^{n}g(x,y)={t}^{n}(2{x}^{3}+3{y}^{2})
$$

and so $g(x,y)$ is not homogeneous.
